gaps.sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I forgot the meeting,' she said. She ___ forgetting the meeting.
gaps.explanation: An apology is reported with 'apologised for + gerund'.

gaps.sentence: 'Sit down, please,' the nurse said to me. The nurse asked me ___ down.
gaps.explanation: Requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive: asked me to sit down.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.
